transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Haan, haan, speaking. Who is this?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Arun from Finserve Collections. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4827. Do you have a moment to speak with me?

Customer: Arre, another call. Look, I know I owe money, okay? I'm not running away. But I don't have it right now.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. I can see here that your account is 87 days overdue with an outstanding balance of 2,85,000 rupees. Your last payment was in June. Can we talk about when you might be able to clear this?

Customer: Two lakh eighty-five thousand? That's... that's not right. When I took the loan, it was 2,50,000. How did it become 2,85,000? What is all this extra amount?

Agent: Okay, so the additional amount includes the interest that has accrued over the overdue period, and there are also some late payment charges that have been applied. Let me break this down for you — the principal remaining is 2,12,000, interest is about 56,000, and penalties are approximately 17,000.

Customer: Penalties? 17,000 in penalties? For what? I didn't miss it on purpose. I lost my job in July, Rajesh. I mean... <interruption> sorry, I lost my job, and I've been trying to find work. How am I supposed to pay penalties when I don't even have income?

Agent: I hear you, Rajesh. Job loss is a difficult situation. But now that you're looking for work, what is your timeline? When do you expect things to improve?

Customer: I should get something in the next month or two. I have some interviews lined up. But listen... <interruption> can we not talk about these penalties? Is there any way to... I mean, can we settle this for less? What's the minimum I can pay to get this closed?

Agent: That's a good question. A settlement could be an option depending on your situation. Before I can present you with a settlement figure, I need to understand better — when you say settlement, are you thinking of paying a lump sum amount once you get employment, or are you asking if we can reduce the total amount owed?

Customer: Both, actually. I mean, I want to know what you're asking for. What is the settlement amount? Can you reduce the penalties? And how much time would you give me?

Agent: Alright. So what I can do is I can calculate a formal settlement offer for you based on your case, but I'll need some more information. First, do you have any funds available right now, or would this settlement need to wait until you secure employment?

Customer: No, no money right now. Everything is stuck. But once I get a job, I can pay. Maybe two months, maximum three months. Can you tell me what number you're looking at? I need to know if it's even possible for me to settle.

Agent: Understood. Let me work on a settlement proposal for you. Before I finalize this, I need to confirm — is this account in your name only, or is there a co-applicant involved?

Customer: Just me. My wife, she doesn't know about this loan actually. I took it for some business investment that didn't work out. So yes, it's just my name.

Agent: Okay, thank you for that clarity. So what I will do is I will prepare a detailed settlement offer with a breakdown of the principal, interest, and any penalties that might be waived or reduced. I'll also include a proposed timeline based on your expected employment. Can I get your email address to send this to you?

Customer: Email is rajesh.kumar.1987@gmail.com. But when will you send it? And how much are we talking about roughly? I need to have some idea.

Agent: I will send you the written settlement offer within 24 hours. As for a rough figure — we're looking at something in the range of 2,10,000 to 2,40,000 depending on how much we can adjust the penalties. The exact amount will be in the email with full details so you can review it properly.

Customer: Okay... okay. So 2,10,000 to 2,40,000. That's still a lot, but at least it's less than 2,85,000. Can you... can you also explain in the email how the interest was calculated? I want to understand what I'm paying for.

Agent: Absolutely, I will include a full ledger and interest calculation breakdown in the email. That way you can review everything at your own pace and then we can discuss next steps. Does that sound fair?

Customer: Yes, yes, that's good. When I get the email, I'll review it and maybe I'll call you back. Or you can call me after, say, a week? I should have more clarity on the job situation by then.

Agent: Perfect. I'll schedule a callback for you exactly seven days from today. In the meantime, you review the settlement offer, and if you have any questions before the callback, feel free to reach out. Can I confirm your mobile number is still 9876543210?

Customer: Yes, that's correct.

Agent: Great, Rajesh. To summarize — I'm sending you a detailed settlement offer with a breakup and timeline within the next 24 hours. You review it, and I'll call you back in seven days. Does that work?

Customer: Yes, that works. Thank you for explaining this properly. I was worried you'd just keep asking for the full amount.

Agent: I understand. We're here to find a solution that works for you. I'll get that email out right away. Take care, Rajesh, and all the best with your job search.

Customer: Thank you. Bye.

Customer: Haan, I know, I know about the EMI. But listen, the account... the account is joint account hai, na. My wife's name bhi hai uspe. I cannot withdraw money or make payment without her signature.

Agent: I see, so it's a joint account with your wife. Where is she right now?

Customer: She is out of station, yaar. She went to her parents' place in Lucknow for her mother's health issue. She'll be back next week, maybe Tuesday or Wednesday. (<interruption>) Sorry, sorry, someone is calling me here...

Agent: No problem, take your time. So if I understand correctly, you need your wife's approval to make this payment? Is that what the bank told you?

Customer: Haan, exactly. The bank account... both our names are there, so both signatures are required for any withdrawal above 50,000 rupees. The EMI amount is 18,500, so technically I can do it, but the thing is... (<interruption>) actually, I need to check with her first because we have other EMIs also. My bike loan, her credit card... everything is connected to this account. So she needs to know before I take the money out.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. Let me ask you this — do you have the funds available right now? Is it just a matter of getting her approval?

Customer: Haan, funds are there, no problem with that. My salary came on the 1st itself. But I'm telling you, without confirming with her, I cannot do it. She will get angry with me, and also she has her own expenses. I don't want to create any family problem, you understand?

Agent: Completely understand, Rajesh. So what we need to do is — you speak with your wife, confirm that she approves the payment, and then you can transfer the money. When do you think she will be back?

Customer: She said Tuesday, probably Tuesday morning. So by Tuesday evening, I can make the payment. Or Wednesday morning at the latest. But I need to speak with her first, explain everything to her. She doesn't know how much the outstanding is now. I think there's some late fee also added?

Agent: Yes, there is a late fee of 2,100 rupees added for the 12-day delay. So your total due is now 20,600 rupees. But this will keep increasing every day. The sooner you can get her approval and make the payment, the better. Can you commit to making this payment by Wednesday latest?

Customer: Haan, haan, I can do that. I will call her tonight itself, explain the situation. She will understand. By Wednesday, definitely the payment will be made. But I need her approval first, na. I cannot just... (<interruption>) sorry, my manager is looking at me. Can I call you back?

Agent: Of course, no problem. But before you go, let me confirm — your wife will be back by Tuesday, and you will call her tonight to get her approval. Then you will make the payment by Wednesday. Is that correct?

Customer: Haan, that's correct. I will make the payment by Wednesday. But only after she agrees. She's the joint holder, so she has equal right to say yes or no.

Agent: Perfect. So I'm going to schedule a follow-up call for Thursday morning. If the payment has been made, we're done. If not, we'll need to discuss further. Is Thursday morning okay for you?

Customer: Thursday morning is fine. By then, the payment will definitely be done. I promise you.

Agent: Thank you, Rajesh. I'm noting down that your wife needs to provide approval, and she will be available from Tuesday onwards. You will contact her tonight, get her agreement, and make the payment by Wednesday EOD. I've scheduled a callback for Thursday at 10 AM to confirm. Please do make this payment on time, as further delays will result in higher penalties and may affect your credit score.

Customer: Haan, I understand. I will do it. Thanks for understanding the situation.

Agent: You're welcome, Rajesh. Take care. We'll speak Thursday morning.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, is this Rajesh Kumar speaking?

Customer: Yes, hello. Who is this calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya from the collections team at FinServe Credit. I'm calling regarding your loan account ending in 4521. Do you have a few minutes to speak with me?

Customer: Ah, yes, yes. I know about this. But I have to tell you something — there is a problem with this account. I've been trying to sort it out for weeks now.

Agent: Okay, I'm listening. What's the issue, Rajesh?

Customer: See, the amount you people are saying I owe — the outstanding balance — it's not correct. I checked with my bank, I checked my records, and I don't understand why this loan is showing on my CIBIL report in the way it is showing. The bureau is reporting it as overdue for 90 days, but I have proof that I made a payment three months back. I even have the UPI reference number.

Agent: I see. Can you help me understand — are you disputing the amount you owe, or are you saying the payment was made but not reflected?

Customer: Both, actually. First, the payment I made — it should have reduced the outstanding balance, but when I checked my CIBIL report online, it's still showing the old amount. And second, the way the bank is reporting this to CIBIL is wrong. They are showing it as overdue when I have already paid.

Agent: Understood. So the bureau data is not matching your payment records. This is definitely something we need to verify. Let me ask you — have you raised a dispute with the credit bureau directly, or are you raising this with us first?

Customer: I did try, but they told me that the lender — that's you, FinServe — has to initiate the correction. They said I need to contact FinServe and ask you to send a correction request. That's why I'm telling you now. I cannot make another payment or commit to anything until this is sorted because my credit report will show wrong information.

Agent: That's a fair point. So you're saying you cannot proceed with a payment commitment until the bureau records are corrected by our end?

Customer: Exactly. How can I make a promise to pay when the bureau is showing false information about me? It's affecting my credit score. And if I make a payment now without the correction, it will still show as overdue on my file, no?

Agent: That's actually a valid concern, Rajesh. Let me be honest with you — what you're asking for requires verification from our side. We need to check our payment records against what CIBIL is showing, and then we would need to file a dispute with the bureau on your behalf. This process takes time — usually 30 to 45 days for the bureau to investigate and correct.

Customer: Thirty to forty-five days? But my loan is overdue. What happens in that time?

Agent: That's a good question. While we're processing the bureau correction, you would still need to make the outstanding payment to stop further penalties and interest accrual. The bureau correction doesn't erase the current outstanding balance — it just corrects the reporting status once we verify your payment was received.

Customer: No, no, no. I don't agree with this. If the bureau is showing wrong information, then how do I know what the real outstanding balance is? You tell me the balance, I check my records, they don't match. The bureau is reporting it wrong. I'm not paying anything until you correct the bureau information first. I want a written confirmation from FinServe that you will file the dispute with CIBIL.

Agent: I understand your frustration, Rajesh. But I need to be clear — I cannot promise a bureau correction without verification. What I can do is escalate your case to our disputes team. They will review your payment proof and our records, compare it with what CIBIL is showing, and then decide if a correction request is warranted. Once that's confirmed, we will file it.

Customer: And how long will that take?

Agent: The internal verification should take about 3 to 5 working days. Then if we find an error, the bureau correction process begins, which is 30 to 45 days.

Customer: <interruption> So basically, you're asking me to wait 5 days first, and I don't know if the correction will even happen. And meanwhile my account is still showing as overdue. This is not acceptable. I want to speak to a supervisor or someone who can actually authorize this.

Agent: I can absolutely escalate this to a supervisor. But I need to make a note in your file — are you refusing to make a payment until the bureau data is verified and a correction is initiated? Or are you open to making a partial payment while we process the verification?

Customer: I'm not refusing to pay. I'm saying I cannot commit to anything until the bureau information is corrected. Once you correct it and I see it updated on my CIBIL, then we can talk about payment. That's my position.

Agent: Noted. I will escalate this to our supervisor and the disputes team right now. Someone from our disputes and verification team will contact you within 2 business days with an update on the bureau reporting verification. Is that acceptable?

Customer: Fine. But I want this escalated properly. Make sure they contact me. And I want written confirmation once the correction is filed with CIBIL.

Agent: Absolutely, Rajesh. I'm noting your request for written confirmation. Our team will reach out soon. Thank you for your time.

Customer: Okay, thank you.

Customer: Arrey, Priya, I know the amount, yaar. The problem is not so simple. I have the money, but... <interruption> sorry, let me explain properly. I have three loans running right now. My bike loan, this personal loan with you, and my home loan EMI. Every month, the total is coming to almost Rs 45,000, and my salary is only Rs 48,000. After expenses and rent, there is almost nothing left.

Agent: I see. So you're saying the total EMI burden is very high compared to your income. Is that correct?

Customer: Exactly! That's what I'm saying. The home loan people, they are calling also, and the bike loan finance company... they are all asking for their money. I cannot pay everyone at the same time, Priya. I have to choose. Last month I gave priority to the home loan because, you know, the house is more important. This month also I'm in the same situation.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. So you're managing multiple EMIs and it's becoming difficult to service all of them together. This is a genuine hardship situation. Can you tell me — are you employed currently, or is there any change in your income?

Customer: No, no, I am employed. I work in a logistics company. But the salary is fixed, and with three loans, it's just not manageable. I am not refusing to pay you, Priya. I want to clear this, but I need some relief. Can we reduce the EMI or something? Can we extend the loan tenure so the monthly payment becomes lower?

Agent: That's a fair request, Rajesh. We do have options like loan restructuring or EMI adjustment, but these require approval from our senior team. Before we escalate this, I need to understand your situation better. Out of your three loans, which one do you consider the most critical to service first?

Customer: <interruption> The home loan, obviously. Because if I miss that, they can take my house. After that, the bike loan because it's a secured asset also. Your personal loan is unsecured, so... I mean, I'm not saying I won't pay, but logically, the secured loans come first, no?

Agent: Yes, I understand your prioritization. That's actually very logical. So the home and bike loan EMIs together come to how much approximately?

Customer: Around Rs 32,000 per month. So for you, I'm left with maybe Rs 10,000 to Rs 12,000 maximum some months. But your EMI is Rs 18,750. So I cannot meet it fully every month.

Agent: I see. So you're in a situation where your total EMI obligations exceed what you can realistically pay from your monthly income. This is what we call overindebtedness. Rajesh, I want to help you. The best option for you would be to speak with our restructuring team. They can look at extending your tenure, which will reduce your monthly EMI. But before I escalate, can I confirm — have you been able to make any payment this month, or are you completely unable to pay right now?

Customer: I managed to pay the home loan and the bike loan. For you, I haven't paid yet. I don't have the full amount right now. Maybe I can arrange Rs 5,000 or Rs 6,000 by the end of this week, but not the full 18,750.

Agent: Okay, Rajesh. So you can offer a partial payment of Rs 5,000 to Rs 6,000 by end of this week, is that right?

Customer: Yes, yes, but Priya, this is not a solution. I need a permanent solution. This partial payment thing, I can do maybe for one or two months, but then what? Next month, same situation. I need the EMI to be reduced permanently. Can you help with that?

Agent: Absolutely, Rajesh. I can definitely escalate your case for restructuring. Customer: Haan, I can try. But I also want to request — please don't keep calling me every day. I know I owe the money. I'm not avoiding it. Just give me time and let the restructuring happen.

Agent: Understood completely. I'll make a note that we're escalating for restructuring, and I'll request that the team holds further calls until they contact you with options. Can I confirm your contact number is still 94XXX22145?

Customer: Yes, that's correct. That's the best number to reach me.

Agent: Perfect, Rajesh. Let me summarize: You're managing three loans totalling Rs 45,000 EMI against a monthly salary of Rs 48,000, leaving you unable to service all EMIs fully.
